Hey everyone! 👋 At AppDev, we don’t just love creating apps—we’re passionate about sharing our craft, too! Our four courses—Intro to Android Development, Intro to Backend Development, Intro to Digital Product Design, and Intro to iOS Development—offer an in-depth dive into the skills we use to bring our apps to life. One of our most revolutionary courses, Intro to Digital Product Design (DPD), has been pivotal in shaping the journeys of many designers here at Cornell—and even beyond, with adoption at places like Harvard. DPD teaches the fundamentals of product design, including how to think about a product, its users, the challenges they face, and how to solve those problems through design. You’ll also learn how to bring your ideas to life using Figma. Our experienced instructors will guide you through every step, and you’ll receive real-time feedback through our critique groups. The best part? You can enroll right now! The course is pass/fail, offers 0–2 credits, and meets on Monday/Wednesday from 7:30–8:20 PM in Statler 398. Not ready to commit or not a Cornell student? You can still audit the class! If you’ve ever considered a career in product design or product management, this is your sign to dive in. Questions? Feel free to reach out to our instructors, Carrie Kim ( kk847@cornell.edu ) or Stefanie Rivera-Osorio ( sar344@cornell.edu ). We hope to see you there! ✨ ...more ...more

I was honored to be invited to present at the 2026 Military Health System Research Symposium MHSRS in Kissimmee, Florida, where I presented research on pharmaceutical supply chain readiness and examined how greater visibility into pharmaceutical sourcing, manufacturing dependencies, and potential supply chain chokepoints can help strengthen military health readiness and national security. This research was made possible through the extensive effort of my brother, 2LT Massimo S. Qasemi , and Colonel (Ret) Victor Suarez from the The Council on Strategic Risks .

I’m very proud to say that this morning I graduated Magna Cum Laude with distinction in research from Cornell CALS (cheered on by Lisa Fortier Bridgette Nixon Nicole Nixon Halana Illig Brendan Maloney ) Entering Cornell as a sophomore transfer from Binghamton University, I was worried I would be behind, overwhelmed, and alone. While there may have been a couple days those feelings came to fruition, the ithaca community, Cornell Faculty, rare sunny days, and the academic spirit of Cornell, allowed me to find joy in being challenged. I chose a major unique to Cornell, Biology and Society. This attempts to combine traditional biology with perspectives from the social sciences that examine the history, structure, and ethics within science, while simultaneously allowing for deep exploration into biological disciplines of your choosing. This interdisciplinary framework I was allowed to navigate is exactly why I chose Cornell, no stone was left unturned. I may not have gotten better everyday, but I never stopped trying. Everything I’ve learned here has made me feel confident I can excel wherever I end up. If I’m back here for vet school, expect more of the same😎

📣 Year one at Georgia Tech is officially in the books! I'm excited to share what's next :D This summer, I'm joining Ramp in NYC as a Backend Software Engineering intern on the Procurement-to-Payment Intelligence team. My first four days in the Big Apple have already been incredible, and I'm very glad to have amazing support from my manager (Andrew Kou), skip manager ( Jacob Forster ), and the rest of the team. Looking forward to gaining firsthand experience developing AI-native platforms. Looking back, this semester was FULL of awesome memories and experiences. Just to name a few of my favorites: • Traveling to Houston for the FIRST Robotics World Championship as a mentor for my team (and winning States 🎉 ) • Developing software with Luke McKay , under the guidance of Thomas González Roberts , to help researchers and policymakers understand airspace restrictions caused by space launch operations • Writing a 1,600-word essay in German on how the media nurtured a societal sense of nostalgia for the past following German reunification Huge thanks to everyone who opened doors and supported me throughout this journey, especially mentors Sid Thota, Ryan McHale, Christopher Wilson, and Luis R. , as well as professors Britta Kallin , Thomas González Roberts , and Harish Ravichandar , and my Ramp recruiters Angela Wu , Cat Choy , and Gloriaivett M. On to year two!
Grateful for the opportunity to share and reflect on how DEA has shaped me over the years. Thankful for all the people and experiences that have been part of this incredible journey!
